# NOAA MPA Inventory

The [NOAA Marine Protected Areas Inventory](https://marineprotectedareas.noaa.gov/dataanalysis/mpainventory/) hosts a publicly available Downloadable GIS data link. The link I'm using here was the inventory as it stands in November 2026, which was last updated in 2023 :

<https://marineprotectedareas.noaa.gov/media/data/NOAA_Marine_Protected_Areas_Inventory_2023.zip>

The following code downloads the GIS data to the input folder and unzips it

```{r}
# point to the GIS download link
noaa_mpa_url <- paste0("https://marineprotectedareas.noaa.gov/media/data/NOAA_Marine_Protected_Areas_Inventory_2023.zip")

zip_path <- here::here("input", "noaa_mpa_2023.zip")
input_path <- here::here("input")

download.file(noaa_mpa_url, zip_path, mode = "wb")
unzip(zip_path, exdir = input_path)

# delete the .zip 
file.remove(zip_path)
```

The following code downloads the .xlsx metadata

```{r}
noaa_mpa_metadata <- paste0("https://marineprotectedareas.noaa.gov/media/data/NOAA_Marine_Protected_Areas_Inventory_2023.xlsx")

download.file(noaa_mpa_metadata, )


```

Examine .gdb

```{r gdb-path}
# Find folders ending in .gdb
folders <- list.dirs(
  input_path,
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)

gdb_path <- folders[grepl("\\.gdb$", folders, ignore.case = TRUE)]

gdb_path
```

A geodatabase can contain multiple layers. Examine available layers and geometry types.

```{r gdb-layers}
layers <- st_layers(gdb_path)
layers
```

| Output | What it means |
|:---|:---|
| `layer_name: NOAA_MPA_Inventory` | The exact layer name you can pass to `st_read()`. |
| `geometry_type: Multi Polygon` | Each feature can contain multiple separate polygon pieces—for example, disconnected protected areas represented by one record. It does not mean each piece is a separate row. |
| `features: 979` | There are 979 spatial records in this layer. That is not necessarily the number of distinct sites; check the site identifiers before treating it as a site count. |
| `fields: 35` | Each feature has 35 non-geometry attribute fields describing it. |
| `crs_name: WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator` | The coordinate reference system is Web Mercator, also called EPSG:3857. It uses projected coordinates in metres rather than longitude/latitude in degrees. |

```{r}
noaa_mpa <- st_read(
  dsn = gdb_path,
  layer = "NOAA_MPA_Inventory"
)

names(noaa_mpa)
```

```{r}
noaa_mpa_wa <- noaa_mpa |> 
  filter(State == "WA")
```

```{r}
plot(st_geometry(noaa_mpa_wa))
```
